prerequisites: Ability to read and understand documentation written in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Familiarize the student with the general functioning and organization of the Internet network.
Enable the student to make informed selections of application technologies in the deployment of heterogeneous networks and their application to a communication infrastructure design.
Provide the student with an overview of next-generation Internet technologies and protocols.
Introduce the student to concepts related to the convergence of communication infrastructures and service integration.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Internet network architecture. Convergent networks.
Operation of the Internet network with IPv6

assessment_methods.method: Theory exam (combined test and theoretical-practical questions)
Continuous evaluation of laboratory practices (or practical exam)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as 0.5 x Continuous Laboratory Practice Evaluation (PL) + 0.5 x Theory Exam (TE), provided that a minimum of 5 out of 10 points is achieved in both PL and TE. If any part is not passed, the final grade will be the highest score of the unpassed parts. To pass the course, students must complete all requested tasks/projects, attend all practice sessions (for ordinary call), achieve a grade equal to or greater than 5 in each task and the final evaluation test, and obtain a final course grade equal to or greater than 5. Grades for passed blocks are saved between calls within the same academic year.
